statement: Under matched thinking-token budgets across Qwen3, DeepSeek-R1-distill and Gemini 2.5, a single agent matched or beat five MAS designs (sequential, subtask-parallel, roles, debate, ensemble) on multi-hop QA; MAS only became competitive when the single agent context was heavily corrupted.
uncertainty: Text-only multi-hop QA, no tools; not open-ended science; budget control on Gemini approximate.

statement: The best-known research-scaffold gain (multi-agent beat single-agent Opus 4 by 90.2% on an internal research eval) was not budget-matched; the same authors report token usage alone explains 80% of BrowseComp variance and MAS use ~15x chat tokens.
uncertainty: Internal eval, not public; the 80% figure is on BrowseComp, not the research eval.

statement: On ResearchClawBench (40 paper-grounded open-ended research tasks), holding the backbone fixed at GPT-5.4, scaffold choice moves scores by about -2.5 to +3.5 points over a plain ReAct harness (15.3); the best multi-agent scaffold (EvoScientist v0.1.1, 18.8) is statistically indistinguishable in practice from a single-agent coding CLI (Codex, 18.4), while another multi-agent scaffold (ARIS, 13.6) is below the harness. Every system is far below the 50-point re-discovery bar.
uncertainty: Budgets and tools were not matched; single-run scores without CIs; multi-agent labels taken from the scaffolds own paper titles; 40 tasks only.

statement: On the same benchmark, score has only a weak positive relationship with cost or runtime, so extra compute spent by heavier scaffolds is not reliably converted into better science.
uncertainty: Correlation over heterogeneous systems; not a controlled budget sweep.

statement: In the only large tool-using study with prompts, tools and compute ceilings held constant (260 configurations, 6 agentic benchmarks), the mean multi-agent effect was 0.0% with a CI spanning -59% to +77%: large gains on decomposable research-like analysis (Finance Agent, +81% centralized), modest gains on web deep-search (BrowseComp-Plus, up to +9%), and losses on sequential planning and software engineering. Gains shrink once the single agent scores above ~45%.
uncertainty: No scientific-discovery benchmark included; small reasoning budgets (~4.8k tokens); Finance Agent n=50; prompts not tuned per architecture.

statement: The strongest science-specific evidence for a multi-agent advantage (AutoScientists vs single-agent Autoresearch, same model backend and GPU budget) shows +8.3 leaderboard-percentile points on BioML-Bench and continued improvement where the single agent stalls, but it holds experimental compute fixed, not LLM tokens (the team uses more), and from a fresh baseline the single agent ended marginally better given more experiments.
uncertainty: Single paper by system authors; overlapping SEs on 24 tasks; n=1 runs for ablations; token budget not matched.

statement: Co-Scientist, the flagship multi-agent scientific-hypothesis system, beats single frontier models in its own Elo tournament only by scaling test-time compute, and its authors note single reasoning models were competitive at much lower compute.
uncertainty: Self-evaluated Elo; small expert panel; no matched-budget arm.

statement: No inspected study runs a multi-agent research scaffold against a single tool-using frontier model on open-ended scientific research with both tools and LLM-token budgets matched: the matched-compute study uses non-science benchmarks, the science benchmark does not match budgets, and science MAS papers match at most experimental compute.
uncertainty: Absence claim based on a limited search; a matched study may exist that was not found.

statement: On data-driven scientific coding tasks, giving a single model an execute-and-fix loop nearly doubles success over one-shot prompting, while a heavier general agent framework (OpenHands) solved fewer tasks at 17x the cost: the gain comes from tool feedback, not scaffold complexity.
uncertainty: 2024-era models (Claude 3.5 Sonnet); OpenHands is a single-agent framework, so this is not a MAS test.

statement: Contradiction: under matched budgets a single agent dominates multi-hop QA, yet under matched tools and compute multi-agent centralized coordination gains +81% on Finance Agent. The likely reason is task structure: decomposable, parallel information gathering favors MAS; sequential reasoning over one context favors a single agent. Open-ended science mixes both.
uncertainty: Explanation is the authors hypothesis (decomposability), supported within one study; not tested on science tasks.

statement: Internal tension in the strongest pro-MAS science result: the headline says the team reached a target loss 1.9x faster, but in the appendix trajectories from the same start the single-agent loop finished at 0.9773 vs 0.9777 for the team (more experiments, lower is better). The MAS edge is clearest only after the single agent has plateaued.
uncertainty: Different experiment counts (83 vs 71); differences sit near the stated noise floor.
